name: Asylum / Refugee Status (CONARE)

requirements.blocker_text: Under the Organic Law on Refugees or Refugees and Asylees or Asylees (LORRAA), the National Commission for Refugees (CONARE) -- created under Hugo Chavez's government and now over 20 years old -- decides refugee status determinations, cessation, loss of status, and repatriation matters, applying Venezuelan law together with applicable international treaties. CONARE operates regional offices in Caracas, Tachira (San Cristobal), Apure (Guasdualito), and Zulia (Maracaibo), and issues provisional documentation during processing; SAIME handles identity documents for recognized refugees.
requirements.fix_path: Apply to CONARE at its Caracas headquarters or a regional office (Tachira, Apure, or Zulia).

evidence_required.document: Application to CONARE with grounds for protection

sources.title: Ministry of Popular Power for Foreign Relations, Venezuela (mppre.gob.ve) -- official CONARE page: its LORRAA legal basis, functions, and regional office structure
UNHCR Venezuela -- corroborates CONARE's role as governing body for international protection, its regional offices, and SAIME's role in documenting recognized refugees

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Venezuela). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- direct government sourcing (mppre.gob.ve, tier 1), corroborated by UNHCR. GENUINE, UNUSUAL DUAL ROLE WORTH NAMING PROMINENTLY: Venezuela is simultaneously (a) the country from which over 7 million people have fled since the mid-2010s, making it overwhelmingly a refugee-SOURCE country in the current moment, and (b) a country with its own real, decades-old CONARE apparatus that historically received refugees fleeing Colombia's internal armed conflict and, per its legal mandate, continues to formally exist and process claims today. Neither source located in this build provided current inbound-refugee population figures for Venezuela itself (as distinct from the much larger, well-documented figures for Venezuelans hosted elsewhere) -- disclosed as a gap, not assumed to be zero. A search result headline reviewed in passing ('Venezuela rejects the use of the term refugee as it is a weapon of aggression') suggests the prior Maduro government was politically resistant to 'refugee' framing in some contexts -- not independently verified or elaborated on in this build, but flagged given the political sensitivity, and worth revisiting under the current Rodriguez-led transitional government (see ve_visitor_visa.json's notes for the fuller political context). Neither source detailed a specific process timeline -- disclosed as unconfirmed. family_can_work left null since neither source addressed dependents' work rights specifically.
